resources.string: Checks GitHub once a day when you\'re online. GitHub receives your IP address and the update request. Updates download only when you choose.
Tell me about newer versions nearby

When two phones connect, each tells the other which MeshLive release it runs, in the signed greeting they already exchange (never in what a phone broadcasts). If a connected phone has a newer one you see a quiet note on the home screen; nothing is downloaded or installed. On a live stream that greeting is not encrypted, so anyone listening nearby can read the release too. Turning this off also stops your phone from telling others its release, except while Use Wi-Fi for faster connections is on: then it still tells it on live streams and when it relays a call.
A friend nearby has a newer MeshLive. Tap to see how to get it.

MeshLive can ask GitHub once a day, while you are online, whether a newer version has been published.

GitHub then sees your phone's internet address and that it asked about MeshLive. Nothing else about you is sent.

Nothing is downloaded until you tap, and nothing is installed without your confirmation. You can change this any time in Settings.
This update needs a newer version of Android than this phone has.
Another update, call or live session is running. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
